oneOf.description: A remembered decision answered on a person's behalf.

An actor that acted on another machine, read out of an export. The
original travels for the record; nothing here acted.

Agent.description:
A durable agent record. This is authoritative state; the model is never
asked to remember any of it.

archived.description:
Cleared out of the live view (issue #18). A durable mark on a
finished agent: it stays in the store, in reports and in replay, and
only the default view filter hides it.

engine_sent.description:
Per-agent layers `engine_session` has already been sent, hashed. Read
through [`Agent::engine_sent_layers`].

engine_session.description:
Session id of an external engine (Claude Code, Codex) that carries this
agent's conversation between turns. `None` for API-driven agents.

engine_usage.description:
What `engine_session` had counted for itself when this agent last
billed it. Read through [`Agent::engine_session_usage`], which
discards a record belonging to any other session.

fallbacks.description:
Models to try, in order, when `model` fails with a retryable error or
its provider is backed off (VISION §4.5). Empty for most agents.

inbox_cursor.description: Inbox items with seq <= cursor have been rendered into a turn.

paused.description:
VISION §3.1: an operator pause, durable across restarts and orthogonal
to the status. A paused agent is never dispatched; its inbox fills.

paused_via.description:
VISION §3.8: set exactly when `paused` and the hold came from a
`--subtree` pause, naming the agent that pause is rooted at (possibly
this one). A subtree hold reaches children created under it and is
lifted by the matching subtree resume; a plain pause holds this agent
alone and leaves this `None`.

restarted_as.description:
The agent that took over from this one after it failed or was
cancelled. Set once: a second restart would fork the history.

restarted_from.description: The failed or cancelled agent this one was restarted from (§3.8).

resume_wait.description:
A wait the scheduler cut short (a person spoke, a child failed).
Restored after the turn unless the agent decides otherwise.

status_since.description: Start of the current continuous status kind; absent for unknown historical state.

AgentAttention.description: A failed agent, or one blocked on something only the operator can clear.

concurrency.description:
At most this many of the agent's descendants, at any depth, run at
once; the rest queue. Never counts the agent itself. `None` (the
shipped default, matching what an omitted field deserializes to)
leaves the whole subtree bounded only by the daemon's global limit -
a nonzero default here would be a WHOLE-SUBTREE cap, not a per-level
one, and would starve every grandchild once it filled (issue #20's
fix round). Set explicitly, it bounds a supervisor's entire subtree,
so pick it for the fan-out you actually want below that supervisor,
not per level.

cost_budget.description: Total spend in US dollars across the agent and its subtree.

deadline.description:
Wall-clock instant after which the agent stops (§3.1). Absolute, so
an orchestrator extends it by setting a later one.

instructions.description: Role- or task-specific instructions layered under the harness policy.

leaf.description: A leaf cannot create children and receives fewer coordination instructions and tools.

long_lived.description:
Stay alive after the current task completes and wait for more work
(a chat root or a long-lived steward). Delegated workers default to false.

max_turns.description: Hard stop on turns; `None` means unbounded.

token_budget.description: Total token budget across the agent and its subtree.

depth.description: Depth below the run's root, so a text rendering can indent the tree.

subtree_usage.description: This agent's spend plus every descendant's.

AgentPatch.description: Partial update to a live agent. Only set fields change.

concurrency.description: Cap on descendants running at once; 0 clears it.

cost_budget.description: Spend limit in US dollars over the agent and its subtree.

deadline.description:
Wall-clock stop for the agent: `{"set": <rfc3339>}` moves it,

fallbacks.description: Replaces the fallback chain; an empty list clears it.

long_lived.description: Stay alive after the current task and wait for more work.

network.description: Scope knobs; both must still narrow the parent's scope.

include_archived.description:
Include agents cleared from the view. Off by default, so a client
that has not heard of archiving sees the cleared view (issue #18).

AgentStats.description: Lifetime token counters and activity stats.

context_tokens.description: Latest reported context input, separate from cumulative billing usage.

oneOf.description:
Read out of another daemon's export. Terminal by construction: an

What approval policy an agent gets when nothing else decides one. The

EngineSentLayers.description:
The per-agent context layers an engine session has already been sent, as
digests of their rendered text.

An engine session ordinarily retains every user turn it was sent, so a
layer whose text has not changed since it was last sent is normally
already in front of the model; sending it again would duplicate it in a
conversation that keeps both copies (#92). That guarantee ends at the
engine's own context compaction - Claude Code's recorded system prompt is
reused only "until the conversation is compacted" - which can replace a
retained turn with a summary the model never sees again as the original
text. Aether requests its own compaction first in the common case, and
`turn_engine` clears this record on a sharp context drop as a cheap bound
against the other order, but neither proves the engine's compaction never
wins the race.

The session id is part of the record: a cleared or replaced session
retains nothing, so its digests must not gate the next turn.

layers.description: Layer kind -> digest of the exact text sent for it.

EngineSessionUsage.description:
An engine session's own cumulative token counters, as it last reported
them, tagged with the session they belong to.

Codex counts a *thread*, not a turn: the counters it reports on a resumed
thread include every earlier turn. Persisting the last reading is what
lets the next turn bill `total - this` instead of the thread's history.
The session id is part of the record so a cleared or replaced session
cannot be billed against another session's counters.

A container per call, with the workspace mounted writable at the same
path, everything else in scope mounted read-only, and network per the
scope's policy.

ExhaustionClass.description:
The subset of [`ModelErrorClass`] a probe can recover from. `ContextLimit`
is deliberately unrepresentable: it is not credits, and waiting cannot fix it.

artifact_payloads.description: Artifacts whose payload was still on disk and travelled with them.

FailureLine.description: What failed, and what it was. Every failure in the run, in order.

kind.description: The event type that carried it, e.g. `tool.failed`.

FallbackRecord.description:
The last time a turn gave up on a provider and moved to the next link of
its chain.

class.description:
The normalized class that caused the move, when an error did. A link
skipped because its provider was already backed off carries none.

reason.description: Why the turn left, in one line.

to.description: The link that took the turn over.

ahead.description: Commits the branch has that its upstream lacks; absent without an upstream.

behind.description: Commits its upstream has that the branch lacks; absent without an upstream.

branch.description: Current branch; absent when detached or not a repository.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes to tracked files, or untracked files.

head.description: Abbreviated commit of `HEAD`, when there is one.

modified.description: Tracked paths changed in the work tree but not staged, conflicts included.

repository.description: Whether the directory is inside a git work tree at all.

root.description: Top level of the work tree; absent when not a repository.

staged.description: Paths with changes staged in the index.

untracked.description: Untracked paths that are not ignored.

GithubDispatchMode.description: How a repository's accepted requests reach an agent.

oneOf.description:
Deliver every trigger to the fixed, operator-chosen `agent`. Stale if
that agent pauses or goes terminal; an operator must repoint it.

Create an Aether-managed checkout and agent for each issue/PR thread.
The daemon's current model, approval, and network defaults apply.

Deliver to (or spawn, the first time or after the previous one went
terminal) a durable agent keyed by (repository, issue/PR number), so
the watcher heals itself instead of pointing at a dead agent forever.

agent.description:
Existing agent chosen by the operator; GitHub cannot select its target.
Required when `dispatch` is `Fixed`; ignored under `Thread`.

allowed_users.description:
GitHub logins allowed to dispatch, stored lowercase. Absent allows any
writer; a listed login must still pass the write-permission check.

dispatch.description: How a matched request picks its target agent.

repository.description: Explicit GitHub.com `owner/name`, not a URL or a local path.

operator_users.description:
GitHub logins whose own requests carry operator authority on every
watched repository, stored lowercase. Absent trusts nobody that far.

pairing_open.description: Whether a pairing is open for a device to claim.

status.description: Always `ok`: a daemon that cannot answer does not answer.

device.description:
A paired device's answer to the challenge the remote carrier sent.
Other transports ignore it.

token.description:
Presented on a transport that has no other authorization - the TCP
listener. The Unix socket ignores it: its file mode is the boundary.

HttpErrorCode.description: Why an HTTP request was refused. See the table in docs/remote.md.

IdempotencyKey.description: What makes two calls the same effect.

InboxItem.description: One delivered item. `seq` is per-agent and strictly increasing.

oneOf.description:
A descendant parked on provider exhaustion; it probes and resumes by
itself, so the recipient is informed rather than asked to act.

The same descendant's provider answered again and its turn continues;
informational, so it never interrupts a wait.

operator.description:
Set only by the daemon's GitHub watcher, for a request it verified
as written by an operator login. Never read from `payload`.

oneOf.description: A bare wake with a reason (deadline passed, operator nudge).

Invocation.description: The result of sending a snapshot to a model.

InvocationSnapshot.description:
Everything sent to the model on one turn, frozen before the request.

Remote inference is not deterministic, so this does not promise replay.
It promises reconstruction: every input the model received, and the
adapter and capability profile that shaped the wire request, are here.

adapter.description: Protocol adapter and its version, e.g. `anthropic-messages/1`.

capabilities.description: The capability profile in force when the request was built.

layers.description: System layers in render order; their `text` concatenates to the system prompt.

memory_ids.description: Memories retrieved into the context, by id.

LayerKind.description: The ordered context layers. Order is the order they are rendered.

LayerPlacement.description: Where a layer's text reached the model on this turn.

oneOf.description:
In the system prompt, where the layer was rendered - also the default
for a hoistable layer that had no text to place this turn, so it
means "not hoisted", not necessarily "sent as system text" (#92).
Hoisted into the last user message, whose text carries it instead.
Not sent at all: an engine session already holds this exact text.

holder.description: Opaque identity of the process or worker holding the lease.

LowDisk.description:
The filesystem holding the daemon's data is below its floor: new turns
wait until it has room again. Turns already running carry on.

path.description: Where free space was measured: the store.

McpServerHealth.description: A server's health as of the last contact attempt.

checked_at.description: When the state was last established.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, when it did.

McpServerState.description: Whether a configured server is usable right now.

oneOf.description: Configured, not contacted yet.
Connected, tools discovered.
The last attempt failed; the tools are not offered to any agent.

McpToolInfo.description: One tool a server offers, as Aether will expose it.

declared.description: True when the class came from config rather than the conservative default.

side_effect.description: How the call is classed: declared in config, else conservative.

MemoryCandidate.description: A proposed memory. Admission decides whether it becomes a record.

confidence.description: 0.0 to 1.0: how sure the author is.

importance.description: 0.0 to 1.0: how much it should influence future work.

supersedes.description: The record this one replaces, when the author knows.

actor.description: Authenticated actor recorded by the runtime, never supplied with content.

source.description: The committed note this came from, for repository knowledge.

include_forgotten.description:
Include memories a person curated out. A browser wants them; nothing
a model sees ever does.

provenance_agent.description: Who recorded the memory, not which agents may retrieve it.

forgotten_at.description:
Curated out. The record stays - history is never deleted - but it is
never retrieved again.

pinned.description: Kept in front of the model: a pinned memory outranks the rest.

retracted.description:
Set when a sweep curated it out rather than a person. `None` is a
person's decision, which outranks the file for good.

oneOf.description:
A repository's notes for one role family: agents in repository `id`
whose role is `role` or extends it at a dot (see [`role_families`]).
Recorded by `root` for itself and every agent beneath it.

MemorySource.description:
A committed file a memory was read from, and the commit it was read at.
The commit is absent when the tree is not a git repository, or git is not
on the machine: the note still stands, its version is just unknown.

file.description: Path relative to the repository root.

Message.description: One turn of conversation as the model sees it.

MessageDelivery.description: One agent's copy of a fanned-out message.

Milestone.description: One line of the run's story: the events a person would want to see.

MissedRunPolicy.description:
When several occurrences elapsed between scheduler ticks, coalescing
delivers one trigger; skipping advances the clock without delivering one.
A tick that is late by less than one recurrence still delivers normally.

ModelCost.description: Price per million tokens in USD.

ModelCostTier.description: Rates for an entire request whose prompt exceeds `prompt_tokens`.

ModelErrorClass.description: Normalized failure class. Every adapter maps its provider's errors here.

oneOf.description: Missing, invalid or expired credentials.
Credentials lack permission for this model or feature.
Provider credits or spending allowance exhausted; fallback may recover.
Provider subscription/session/day/week allowance exhausted.

configured.description: Whether credentials resolve for the provider right now.

ModelRef.description: A provider-qualified model name, rendered as `provider/model`.

NewApprovalRule.description: A remembered decision written directly, without answering a call first.

OperatorMemoryScope.description: Operator applicability, not authorship. Repository identity is resolved by the runtime.

OperatorMemorySpec.description: A person supplies content and applicability, never fabricated provenance.

OperatorOrigin.description: Server-observed connection identity, never a bearer token or client-supplied name.

oneOf.description: A paired remote device, named as the daemon enrolled it.

code.description: The single-use code, as printed or read from the URL fragment.

public_key.description:
The device's raw P-256 public key (65-byte uncompressed point),
base64url without padding.

phrase.description: Show it; the operator compares it with the host's.

device.description: Present once `enrolled`: the identity to authenticate as.

Pairing.description: One pairing attempt. Reply to the four pairing commands.

code.description: The single-use code. Present only in the reply to `start_pairing`.

role.description: The role the device is enrolled with on confirmation.

url.description: The pairing URL with the code in its fragment. Same presence as `code`.

PairingCandidate.description: The device asking to be enrolled, as the host must confirm it.

fingerprint.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw public key.

phrase.description: Shown on both screens; the operator confirms they match.

oneOf.description: Waiting for a device to claim the code.
A device claimed the code; waiting for the host to confirm.

path.description:
Absolute for `directory`; relative to the workspace for
`workspace_file`. A directory ends in `/`.

oneOf.description: Directories anywhere on the host, for choosing a workspace.
Files and directories inside `workspace`, for mentions.

pending_unlinks.description: Durable unlink retry records; some may still share a live payload.

staged_publications.description:
Staged files awaiting publication/recovery, possibly still in flight.
No publication leases are acquired or released by preview.

PendingQuestion.description: An agent's question nobody has answered or superseded.

Provenance.description: Where an imported run came from. Absent on a run this daemon ran itself.

source_instance.description: `instance_id` of the store it was exported from.

source_run.description: The run's id in the daemon that exported it.

ProviderBackoff.description: Why a provider is being avoided, and until when.

ProviderHealth.description:
One provider's scheduling picture. Derived state: the scheduler rebuilds
it from the turns in flight and the feedback providers have given.

backoff.description: Set while the scheduler is holding turns back.

last_fallback.description: Where a turn went the last time it gave up on this provider.

limit.description: Configured cap on concurrent turns; `None` leaves it to the global limit.

quota.description: Latest subscription window the provider reported.

recent_errors.description:
Classes this provider has been failing with lately, newest first.
Engines report a message rather than a class, so these cover the
API-model turn path.

running.description: Model turns in flight on this provider right now.

suspended_agents.description: Live agents parked on this provider's exhaustion, waiting to probe it.

ProviderInfo.description:
One provider as a client sees it: what it is, whether it can be used, and
how it is behaving right now. `health` is live scheduler state, so a
provider that has done nothing since the daemon started reads as idle.

auth_source.description: Where the credential came from, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `claude login`.

base_url.description: Endpoint for an HTTP provider; empty for an engine, which owns its own.

engine.description: Inference runs through an official CLI under the person's own login.

family.description:
Declared model family, which chooses the authored profile every model
here is sent: `claude`, `gpt`, `codex`. `None` means no profile at
all. A name, like `protocol`, so the wire type stays free of the
registry. A model may declare its own; this is the provider's.

models.description: Models the registry lists; an open-list provider also takes others.

open_model_list.description: Whether the provider accepts any model id, not only the listed ones.

ProviderUsage.description: Latest normalized account report. The observation time is not a reset time.

PublishArtifact.description:
Publish UTF-8 evidence associated with a durable task. The daemon owns
blob storage and derives the agent/run association from that task.

PushConfig.description: Reply to the push commands: what the daemon sends this device.

enabled.description: Whether the daemon sends notifications at all.

kinds.description: The kinds the asking device is notified about; empty means all.

subscribed.description: Whether the asking device holds a subscription.

vapid_public_key.description:
The VAPID application server key (uncompressed P-256 point,
base64url without padding). Absent while push was never enabled.

PushPayload.description: The decrypted body of one Web Push message.

instance_id.description: The daemon that sent it; a client ignores another instance's.

preview.description: At most 200 characters of content; only with `[remote] push_previews`.

title.description: Fixed text per kind; never transcript content.

url.description:
Where a tap lands: a fragment route of the web app, such as
`#attention?item=apr_...`, relative to the service worker's scope.

auth.description: The subscription's auth secret, base64url without padding.

endpoint.description: The push service URL. Must be https.

p256dh.description: The subscription's P-256 public key, base64url without padding.

QuotaWindow.description:
A subscription usage window as an engine reported it. Opaque JSON on the
wire from the CLI; normalized here so every reader agrees.

used_percent.description: How much of the window is spent, 0-100 (clamped).

window_minutes.description: Length of the window in minutes, when the engine says.

RecoveryClass.description: How an interrupted turn should be handled after a restart.

oneOf.description: No mutating tool was in flight; the agent can simply take another turn.
Retry from the last committed step; in-flight work was safe to repeat.
A side effect may have partially occurred; a human must look.
Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

RememberSpec.description:
How to remember the answer a person just gave. The defaults are the
narrowest reading of it: the answered agent, this tool, and what this
call touched. Anything wider is asked for explicitly.

scope.description: Where it applies; absent means the answered agent alone.

tool_wide.description:
Cover every call of the tool instead of the answered call's argument
and resources.

RemoteSettings.description: The runtime-changeable remote settings, saved whole under a revision.

enabled.description: Whether the remote listener is open.

public_origins.description:
Exact origins browsers reach the listener by, e.g.
`https://host.tailnet.ts.net`. The Host and Origin allowlist.

push.description: Whether the daemon sends Web Push notifications.

error.description: Why the listener is not open although enabled.

listening.description: The address actually bound; absent while the listener is closed.

decided_by.description: Who answered, as an actor label (`user`, `rule:rule_…`).

ReplayContext.description:
The shape of what the model was given. The layer texts are here; the
whole snapshot is a separate record, named so a caller can fetch it.

context.description: What it saw: the context assembled for the model.

from_seq.description:
Sequence range of the events this frame was folded from, so a caller
can jump the live timeline to the same place.

messages.description: What was said, in order - what it was shown and what it answered.

oneOf.description: Reply to `Interrupt`: whether a turn was running to stop.

Reply to `Pause`: the agents it moved, root first, empty when they
were already paused; `mid_turn` names those whose current turn must
finish before the pause takes effect.
One entry per agent a fanned-out message reached, in delivery order.

ResourceHolding.description:
Resource keys one agent's mutating tool call holds for the length of that
call. Two agents never hold conflicting keys at once (VISION §3.6 limit 5).

quarantined.description:
Held for an agent parked for inspection rather than for a running
call: nothing is using the keys, and only a person clears them (§15).

ResourceKey.description:
A resource a call touches, used to decide which calls may run together.
Conventional forms: `file:<absolute path>`, `dir:<absolute path>`,
`repo:<root>`, `network`, `agent:<id>`.

artifact_payload_bytes.description: Projected logical payload bytes, counting shared digests once.

Retraction.description:
Why a repository-knowledge sweep curated a record out: the committed tree
named here no longer states it, so the `file@sha` label it carried is no
longer a promise anyone can check.

Distinct from a person's `forget` on purpose. A person's curation outranks
the file however many times the note comes back; a retraction is undone by
the note reappearing in the tree.

commit.description: The commit whose tree was checked and does not state it.

file.description: The file that stated it, relative to the repository root.

Revocation.description:
Why a rule stopped applying. Kept on the record so the log explains a
decision that would be made differently today.

Role.description:
Opaque role label; an orchestration layer such as Archon gives it meaning.
The harness reads only its dots, to pick a repository's notes for a role
family (`memory::role_families`).

RuleMatch.description:
What a rule matches. An absent field matches anything, so the empty
matcher covers every call — deliberately, so "allow everything for this
run" is expressible without a magic pattern.

argument.description:
Glob over the call's argument (the command for a shell, the path for
a file tool). `*` crosses separators.

resource_prefix.description:
Literal prefix a touched resource key must start with, e.g.
`file:/repo/src`.

oneOf.description: Every agent this daemon runs.
One agent only.
An agent and everything it delegates to.
Every agent in one run.

RunBody.description:
Everything derived from the run's own work. Carries no local sequence
numbers, so two stores holding the same run produce equal bodies once
their ids are put side by side ([`RunReport::canonical_json`]).

duration_ms.description: Wall time from the first event to the last, in milliseconds.

objective.description: The root agent's objective, when the run has one.

open_loops.description: What is still unfinished: live agents, open tasks, pending approvals.

usage.description: Every agent's own usage summed: the run's total spend.

RunListing.description: One row of `aether runs list`, projected from a run's agents and tasks.

agents_imported.description:
How many of `agents` came out of an export. Non-zero means this run
is an archive of another daemon's work, which the listing is the
first place a person would look for.

objective.description: The root agent's task objective, when the run has one.

updated_at.description: When anything in the run last changed.

RunOutcome.description: A run's state, read from its agents rather than declared anywhere.

oneOf.description: At least one agent has not reached a terminal state.

RunReport.description:
A run's report: a header that says which run and when, and a body that
says what happened. Only the body is comparable across stores - the
header carries the local identity.

from_seq.description: Sequence range of the events this was folded from, in this store.

oneOf.description: The first blocker, in the same order as the deletion path.

history_payload_bytes.description:
Serialized payload bytes, excluding indexes and SQLite page overhead.
Zero for protected runs. This is reusable database space, not disk shrinkage.

RunSummary.description: What one run has spent and where that rate leads.

forecast_usd_next_hour.description: What it would have spent after another hour at that rate.

rate_usd_per_hour.description:
Dollars per hour over the run's life so far. Derived from
`usage.cost_usd`, so it is a floor exactly when that is.

Schedule.description:
Timers enqueue work, never authority: targets keep their scope and budgets;
spawned runs get only what an operator could grant via `create_agent`.

last_inbox_seq.description: Delivery schedules: the inbox sequence of the newest trigger.

last_spawned.description: Spawn schedules: the root of the newest spawned run.

spawn.description: Spawn schedules: the template each occurrence starts a run from.

target.description: Delivery schedules: the agent that receives each trigger.

ScheduleOccurrence.description:
History describes delivery or spawning, never claims that a model
completed the requested work. The ids link to the execution trace.

oneOf.description: A spawn schedule started a run: its root agent and task.

Scope.description:
Execution scope: where an agent may act. A first-class runtime attribute,
not prose in a prompt.

allowed_paths.description:
Additional roots the agent may touch besides the workspace, and the
paths it owns: with any set, Aether's built-in shell refuses git commands
that would discard working-tree changes outside them.

backend.description: Where the agent's tools run: the daemon's machine, or a container.

labels.description: Free-form labels an orchestrator may use for limits and routing.

repository.description: Logical repository identifier (a URL or a name) for memory scoping.

workspace_root.description: Root directory tools operate in. Relative tool paths resolve here.

SeedReport.description: What one pass of reading a repository's committed notes did.

found.description: Notes read from the repository's files.

retracted.description:
Seeded before, and no file states it any more: curated out with the
reason, because the label promises the fact can still be checked.

unchanged.description: Already stored word for word; not offered again.

id.description:
The request this answers. Request ids start at 1, so **0 is
reserved**: it is the daemon speaking on its own account rather
than answering anything - the reason a connection is about to
close, or a frame that did not decode. A client keeps it and
reports it instead of a bare disconnect; it never resolves a
waiting request.

oneOf.description:
The remote carrier speaking first: what a device signs to
authenticate its hello. Never sent on the socket or the token listener.

nonce.description: 32 random bytes, base64url without padding. Single use.

SideEffectClass.description:
What a tool does to the world. Drives retry policy, idempotency tracking
and approval requirements.

oneOf.description: Safe to retry any number of times.
Repeating with the same input yields the same end state.
Repeating may compound the effect (append, send, spend).
Reaches outside the workspace: network, external services.

SpawnSpec.description:
Root agent + task each spawn occurrence creates, in a new run. Fields as on
`create_agent`; no parent or existing run.

config.description:
Budgets bound each run. Absolute deadline (stale by run two) and
`long_lived` (keeps run one live, skipping the rest) are refused.

model.description:
Resolved when the schedule is created, so every run uses the model
shown by `get_schedule` rather than whatever the default is later.

objective.description: Each run's task. The occurrence's due time is appended to it.

scope.description: Absent: the daemon's default root scope when each run starts.

SubmissionResolution.description:
What became of a keyed command, as far as the daemon can prove. Each
carries the daemon's `horizon` now; `retained_since` is for people to read.

oneOf.description: It ran. `reply` is what a duplicate under the same key is answered.

It never ran: no receipt, and no receipt recorded since the request's
horizon was ever dropped. Sending it again under the same key is safe.

No receipt, and nothing proves there never was one. Only a person can
decide whether to send it again.

dependencies.description: Tasks that must be terminal before this one can start.

owner.description: Agent executing the task, once assigned.

TaskResult.description: The durable outcome of a task. Cheap to carry in context forever.

ThinkingMode.description:
How the model should think. Adapters honor what the capability profile
supports and report the rest as unsupported.

ThinkingSupport.description: Which thinking controls a model accepts.

oneOf.description: Fixed token budget (`budget_tokens`, `reasoning_effort` mapped to budgets).
Model decides depth; effort steers it.

ToolCall.description: One tool invocation requested by a model.

idempotency_key.description:
What makes this call the same effect as another. Absent for classes
whose outcome is not recorded (see `SideEffectClass::retry_policy`).

provider_call_id.description: Id issued by the provider, echoed in the tool result block.

resources.description: Resources the call will touch, computed by the tool from its input.

ToolExposure.description: Which registered tools an agent may see.

ToolLine.description: One tool's tally across the run.

duration_ms.description:
Time spent inside calls of this tool, successful or failed. A failed
call that never actually ran (`ToolFailed.duration_ms == None`)
contributes nothing, since it has no real time to report.

replayed.description: Answered from a committed outcome; the call did not run again.

content.description: Model-facing text. Large outputs are summarized here and stored as artifacts.

side_effect_occurred.description:
Whether a side effect is known to have occurred. `None` means unknown,
which recovery treats as "needs inspection" for mutating tools.

ToolResult.description: How a tool call in this turn ended.

oneOf.description: Requested, and the log carries no end for it.

duration_ms.description:
`None` when the call never actually ran; see
`EventKind::ToolFailed`. `skip_serializing_if` keeps it absent
on the wire for `None` rather than a literal `null`.

oneOf.description: Answered from a committed outcome; the call did not run again.

ToolResultBlock.description: Content allowed inside a tool result.

ToolSpec.description: Tool definition as exposed to the model.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the tool input.

strict.description: Ask the provider to guarantee schema-valid arguments when it can.

TreeNode.description: One node of the live graph.

subtree_usage.description: Usage rolled up over this agent and its descendants.

waiting_on.description: Tasks this agent is waiting on, resolved from its wait condition.

oneOf.description: The log ends inside this turn: it is the turn in flight.

UnprovenAbsence.description: Why an absent receipt does not prove its key was never executed.

oneOf.description: The request named no horizon, so nothing bounds when the key was sent.

The horizon was issued under another ledger: the store was replaced,
restored from before the ledger existed, or its identity changed.

The horizon counts more receipts than the store has recorded: the
store was rolled back to an earlier state.
Receipts recorded after the horizon have been evicted or expired.

Usage.description:
Token accounting for one invocation, or a running total.

`cost_usd` sums invocations with a configured price or provider-reported
cost; `cost_basis` distinguishes those sources and `cost_complete` says
whether any invocations were left out. List prices are estimates, even
when every invocation was priced. A budget enforces on this accounting
bound - an unpriced invocation
cannot make what was already spent smaller - so nothing silently stops
firing when a model or engine reports no price.

cost_basis.description:
Source of the dollar figures, including `estimated_cost_usd` where present.
List-price figures retain their existing budget semantics; this is a label.

cost_complete.description:
Every invocation folded in here could be priced. Once false it never
returns to true: an unknown cannot be recovered by adding to it.

cost_usd.description:
Dollars over the invocations that could be priced. A floor when
`cost_complete` is false.

estimated_cost_usd.description:
Dollars nobody billed, at the list price of the API model behind a
subscription one: an **estimate**, so it sits beside `cost_usd`
instead of in it. No budget reads it, and every surface labels it
([`Self::estimate_said`]). Like `cost_usd` it is a floor - an unpriced
invocation whose model has no known API equivalent adds nothing - and
`None` means nothing here was estimated at all.

UsageWindow.description: One named account limit, including limits outside the preferred scheduling window.

WaitCondition.description:
What a waiting agent is waiting for. A typed expression the scheduler
evaluates; the model never polls. Leaves are single facts, and `Any`,
`All` and `AtLeast` combine them, so "wait for two of these five workers
or a deadline" is a value, not a prompt.

oneOf.description: The task reached a terminal state.
Any inbox item at all.

daemon_protocol_version.description:
Newest version the daemon speaks. Absent from a daemon built before
N-1 support, which only ever matched exactly.

device.description:
The paired device this connection authenticated as. Absent on the
Unix socket and the token listener.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
How long this connection may go without sending a frame before the
daemon closes it. Set on the TCP listener; absent on the socket, which
has no timeout. A client that subscribes and then falls silent must
send [`Command::Ping`] more often than this.

min_protocol_version.description: Oldest version the daemon still serves.

protocol_version.description:
The version in effect for this connection, which is the client's own
when the daemon translated down to it (`compat`).

submission_horizon.description:
Opaque receipt count at the handshake, kept with each keyed send for
[`Command::ResolveSubmission`]. Absent before protocol 18.

Workspace.description: One workspace the daemon knows: it holds or held a root agent.

active_at.description: Latest update of any root agent here; what orders the list.

agents.description: Live agents in trees rooted here.

path.description: Canonical absolute path on the host.
The canonical path, when the input resolved to one.

reason.description: Why not, in one sentence. Absent when `valid`.

valid.description: Whether an agent can be started here.
